_landed_this_round._method: MERGED, not rebased or cherry-picked, and that was a deliberate change of mechanism. The branches left bc4f06e and 4b7f84d while the tip moved through P1-020's ~1,700 lines in apex-agentd; a 12-commit cherry-pick conflicted on its FIRST commit and would have conflicted repeatedly. One merge resolves the same divergence once, keeps every commit message (which is where this program stores its mutation proofs), makes resume.sh's unlanded list exact because the commits become ancestors, and means the next landing of the same branch merges only its new commits instead of re-applying landed patches. Task branch refs were NOT rewritten, so every agent worktree is exactly where its card left it.

The variable is APEX_AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT; APEX_AGENT_SCRATCH no longer exists.

client.rs publish_hook: the tip's signature (takes the whole hook::Observation) won over the branch's seven positional arguments, and carries the branch's new field as obs.test.clone(). apex/src/agent.rs keeps the tip's call site.

_field_contract: resume.sh does os.path.isdir(worktree) and git rev-list origin/<branch>..HEAD, so `worktree` and `branch` must each be ONE value. An agent working two repos records the other in second_worktree/second_branch, which resume.sh ignores. Writing 'a and b' there makes the next report say 'no worktree' for a worktree that is fine.
_findings: ROADMAP/state/FINDINGS-round5.md — three defects found by running the TIP rather than a branch, all three checked to be pre-existing rather than assumed. (1) `apex ai status --json` returns prose, not JSON, on any machine with nvidia-smi installed but no loaded driver: gpu.rs detects 'no NVIDIA' by the binary being ABSENT, but the L16 has /usr/bin/nvidia-smi and it exits 9. Same 'permission denied is not absence' class as the ~14 already found, wearing 'driver not loaded'. Owner: P1-043, i.e. the live p1-039 agent. (2) `apex remote pair|devices|revoke|status|enable` is documented NOWHERE in docs/, and check-doc-verbs.sh structurally cannot catch it -- it validates documented-verb -> real-command, not the reverse. Owner: the next integrate or followups round, against the tip; followups-int3 was deliberately told not to do it from a stale base. (3) THE IMPORTANT ONE: tests/test-privilege-requests.sh is 30/8 on the tip AND 30/8 with the identical eight names in the identical order at the pre-landing tip 4ab5f75, and all eight fail for the same reason as the single cargo test failure that three integration rounds have written off as 'the cgroup/origin artifact' -- a test runner's cgroup reads as scheduled-job, so §7's gate refuses a root approval before the behaviour under test is reached. That is nine unverified assertions across two harnesses, covering the approval path, including 'a denied request cannot be flipped to approved'. Not an artifact; a hole in the harness. p0-014's 3c3abd3 suggests it has already started on this class.
